description: These city-wide heavy rain hazard maps for Herne show where surface flooding is expected, with depth and extent in shades of blue, calculated with hydrodynamic computer models on a digital terrain model to identify main flow paths and depressions. Three one-hour rainfalls were run: a rare 30-year event of 42.8 millimetres, an exceptional 100-year event of 52.5 millimetres and an extreme event of 90 millimetres, and the public sewer network, infiltration and evaporation are not considered by default. The city of Herne published them through the Metropole Ruhr open data portal and Open.NRW as a WMS service, created in June 2018 with metadata updated in March 2026. Coverage: one city, surface flooding only. Access: a free view service, but Open.NRW marks the licence as another closed licence and the openness scale as not open. Caveats: large-scale mapping can overstate local conditions, and the drainage network is ignored. It supports pluvial flood exposure and adaptation planning, and relates to the national BKG heavy rainfall hazard map in the catalogue.
